issues.title: Backfill unit tests for Queue mirrors and remaining Employee-adjacent entities
issues.description:
**Goal:** Close two related unit-test gaps in one sprint — the SQL-side Queue mirror entities (consumed by the four worker services) and the Employee-adjacent entities that the Employee backfill left untested.

## Part A — Queue mirror entities (22 classes, ~49 methods, 0 tests today)

These are the `ORBIT.Model.Queue.*` mirrors that the four worker services drain to send notifications, run OOO, and sync to SQL reporting.

**Test-env constraint:** the unit test environment has **no SQL Server** — only MongoDB. Tests must focus on the in-memory transform (`ToBsonDocument`, projection from source entity, equality with source) rather than actual SQL persistence. Expect ~50% method coverage until a SQL test container is available.

**What will be done:**
- One test file per mirror under `Source/dotnet/ORBIT.Test.Unit/Queue/` (e.g. `Queue/Employee.cs`, `Queue/CustomerRole.cs`, `Queue/NotificationEvent.cs`).
- Always use fully qualified `ORBIT.Model.Queue.<Entity>` — bare `Queue` collides with `System.Collections.Generic.Queue<T>`.
- Cover: projection from the source model entity, `Remove()` idempotency, and BSON round-trip.

## Part B — Supervisor / EmployeeTask / EmployeeAudit gaps

These were left as `Assert.Inconclusive` or skipped in the Employee backfill.

**What will be done:**
- `Supervisor.Transfer` and `Supervisor.Update` — cascade-to-subordinates behavior; assert that subordinate Employee docs pick up the new supervisor projection.
- `EmployeeTask.Save` / `Remove` — lifecycle, queue side effects, cleanup pattern.
- `EmployeeAudit.Save` + `ToBsonDocument` — verify the audit row is written with the expected fields.
- Standard `try/finally` cleanup including `ORBIT.Model.Queue.Employee` and `ORBIT.Model.Queue.CustomerRole` removal.

**Out of scope:** Editing files under `ORBIT.Model/Employee/` or `ORBIT.Model/Notification/` (off-limits per CLAUDE.md). Tests only.

issues.title: Backfill unit tests for Reminder class
issues.description:
**Goal:** Close the standalone unit-test gap on `ORBIT.Model.Reminder` — small but visible coverage hole that affects the profile-update reminder flow.

**Scope:** `Source/dotnet/ORBIT.Model/Reminder.cs` (single class).

**What will be done:**
1. Create `Source/dotnet/ORBIT.Test.Unit/Reminder.cs` (root namespace `ORBIT.Test.Unit`, since `Reminder` lives in the `ORBIT.Model` root).
2. Cover the public surface:
   - `FetchBy` / `FetchById` overloads — assert non-null and filter correctness
   - `Save` — insert + update round-trip, verify `DateCreated` / `TouchedBy` audit fields
   - Any reminder-trigger logic (date-window evaluation, IsActive transitions)
3. Use the Category B scaffold (`[TestInitialize]` / `[TestCleanup]`) since Reminder is standard CRUD without an SQL queue mirror.
4. `Assert.Inconclusive` if no Reminder records are seeded for the test customer.

**Why it's broken out:** The rest of the "specialized models" gap (Dto / Email / Log / X509) is low-value coverage of thin wrappers and is being deferred indefinitely. Reminder is the one class in that group that actually drives user-visible behavior — the profile-update nag flow — so it warrants its own ticket.

Correctly process Mobile Check-In input with no space between number and text
issues.description:
**User Story**
As a user who submits daily status via Mobile Check-In, I want my status to be correctly processed when I submit my status either with or without a space between the status code (1 - 9) and the state abbreviation, when used. 

Reference INC0035071.

When submitting mobile check-in, the user is not including a space between the status and supporting text, e.g. "3MD" instead of "3 MD". This results in the user's input not being processed and the user receiving the response, "We are sorry your location cannot be processed."

This behavior started on 24 April 2026, following the release of ORBIT 3.3.0.1 to production on 24 April.

issues.title: OOO Upload date should be absolute date (not relative)
Notification SMS Verify section appears on each profile page save
issues.description:
The "Notification SMS Verify" section should only appear on a user's profile page after they have edited their profile and modified the Notification SMS number on their profile. 

---

Currently, when a user opens their profile in edit mode and then saves the form, the "Notification SMS Verify" section appears on the page. This happens no matter what fields are edited on the form, and even if no fields are edited. If the user has a Notification SMS number configured, they can use the "resend" option to get a code and clear the section. If they do not have a Notification SMS number configured, there is no way for them to clear the section.

issues.title: Show successful verification confirmation on user profile page
issues.description:
When a user successfully verifies a contact method that requires verification - Notification SMS, Notification email, Mobile Check-In - the user should remain on their profile page and the relevant section of the profile page should change from the "verify" form to an acknowledgement that verification was successful. 

---

Currently, when a user successfully verifies the contact information, the page automatically redirects the user to the ORBIT home page with no confirmation that the verification was successful.

issues.title: Show failed verification on user profile page
issues.description:
When a user enters an incorrect verification code and fails to successfully verify a contact method that requires verification - Notification SMS, Notification email, Mobile Check-In - the user should remain on their profile page and the relevant section of the profile page should change to include a note that the entered code was wrong and to please try again. The rest of the section should remain the same. 

---

Currently, when a user enters an incorrect verification code, they see the standard "your data was not saved" pop up.

issues.title: Notification report (sent notification) view returns 500 when a response has a null Employee
issues.description:
## Summary
Viewing a sent-notification report 500s for the entire page if **any** `NotificationResponse`
in that event has a null/unbound `Employee`. The crash is a `NullReferenceException` thrown
during Razor rendering of the shared partial, so one bad row takes down the whole report.

This item is scoped to **making the view resilient** so a null `Employee` can never again
500 the report. Fixing/preventing the null `Employee` data itself is tracked separately
(see "Follow-up").

## Root cause (confirmed via Azure log stack trace)
`System.NullReferenceException`
→ `Views_Shared_View_NotificationEvent.<>c.<ExecuteAsync>b__0_1(NotificationResponse t)`
→ `System.Linq.Enumerable.EnumerableSorter.ComputeKeys(...)`

The exception originates in the response-table sort in
`Source/dotnet/ORBIT.Web/Views/Shared/View/NotificationEvent.cshtml`:

```csharp
.OrderBy( t => t.Employee.NameLast + t.Employee.NameFirst )
This appears in both the response-required branch (~line 108) and the non-response-required
branch (~line 151). When t.Employee is null, the OrderBy key selector throws before a
single row renders. The same null deref also exists on the per-row reads inside both loops
(Employee.NameLast, Employee.NameFirst, Employee.Id, Employee.UniqueId).
```
Because the failure happens during view rendering (after the controller action returns), it is
not captured by the in-app SystemLog writer — it only appears in Azure/Kestrel logs.

Affected paths
Both routes render the same shared partial and are affected:

/setting/customer/{id}/notification/view/{subId} (Customer area)
/notification/event/view/{id} (Notification area)
File to change: Source/dotnet/ORBIT.Web/Views/Shared/View/NotificationEvent.cshtml

## Acceptance Criteria (Gherkin)

```
Feature: Sent-notification report tolerates responses with a missing Employee
  As a notification manager
  I want the sent-notification report to render even when a response record has no Employee
  So that one bad record does not make the entire report unavailable

  Background:
    Given I am authenticated and authorized to view notification reports
    And a notification event exists with one or more sent responses

  Scenario: Report renders when one response has a null Employee (response required)
    Given the notification event has "Response Required" set to Yes
    And at least one of its responses has a null Employee
    And at least one of its responses has a valid Employee
    When I open the notification report for that event
    Then the page returns HTTP 200
    And the response table renders all rows
    And rows with a valid Employee show the person's name
    And rows with a null Employee render without throwing and show a placeholder instead of a name

  Scenario: Report renders when one response has a null Employee (no response required)
    Given the notification event has "Response Required" set to No
    And at least one of its responses has a null Employee
    When I open the notification report for that event
    Then the page returns HTTP 200
    And the response table renders all rows
    And rows with a null Employee render without throwing and show a placeholder instead of a name

  Scenario: Report renders when every response has a null Employee
    Given all of the notification event's responses have a null Employee
    When I open the notification report for that event
    Then the page returns HTTP 200
    And the response table renders one row per response without throwing

  Scenario: Sorting is stable when some responses have a null Employee
    Given the notification event has a mix of responses with and without a valid Employee
    When I open the notification report for that event
    Then the page returns HTTP 200
    And rows with a valid Employee are ordered by last name then first name
    And rows with a null Employee are grouped together and do not break the sort

  Scenario: Existing behavior is unchanged when all responses have a valid Employee
    Given every response in the notification event has a valid Employee
    When I open the notification report for that event
    Then the page returns HTTP 200
    And the report renders exactly as it does today
```
## Technical Notes / Implementation Hints    
Null-guard the OrderBy key selector in both branches, e.g. OrderBy( t => (t.Employee?.NameLast ?? "") + (t.Employee?.NameFirst ?? "") ).
Null-guard every per-row notificationResponse.Employee.* access inside both loops (name, Id for the profile link, UniqueId). Render a clear placeholder (e.g. "Unknown employee") and skip/disable the profile link when Employee is null.
Keep the change confined to the view; do not alter model/query behavior in this item. Source/dotnet/ORBIT.Web/... is editable (this is NOT under the off-limits ORBIT.Model/Notification paths).
The defensive rendering must hold regardless of how a response came to have a null Employee, so the report can never again 500 on this condition.
## Out of Scope   
Identifying, repairing, or preventing the null Employee data itself (follow-up below).
The separate exception-handler misconfiguration that turns the 500 into a raw error page instead of the friendly error page (track separately if desired).
## Definition of Done   
Notification report renders HTTP 200 for events containing null-Employee responses, for both response-required and non-response-required events, on both affected routes.
No regression for events where all responses have a valid Employee.
Verified locally against a seeded event containing at least one null-Employee response.
## Follow-up (separate work items, not this one)   
Prevent null Employee from being persisted on a NotificationResponse (validate at all write paths; reconcile the divergent Dto/ToBsonDocument storage shapes).
Data cleanup: identify and repair existing responses with a missing/unbound Employee.

issues.title: Backfill unit tests for the Log family entities
issues.description:
**Goal:** Close the unit-test gap on the `Log<T>` family of entities, which currently have **no** test coverage.

**Classes in scope (5):**
- `ApplicationLog` — `ORBIT.Model/Log/Application.cs`
- `SystemLog` — `ORBIT.Model/Log/SystemLog.cs`
- `OooLog` and `OooLogParent` — `ORBIT.Model/Log/Ooo.cs`
- `ResponseTime` — `ORBIT.Model/Log/ResponseTime.cs`

**Why these are testable now:** `Log<T>` persists through `GetCollection()` (MongoDB only) — no SQL Server dependency — so unlike the Queue mirrors (#1350) these can be exercised fully in the local Mongo unit-test environment.

**Out of scope:** `ReminderLog` (`Log/Reminder.cs`) is tracked separately under #1352.

**What will be done:**
- Test files under `Source/dotnet/ORBIT.Test.Unit/Log/` (namespace `ORBIT.Test.Unit.Log`).
- Cover the read paths (`FetchActive()` / `FetchAll()` / `FetchBy(...)` / `FetchById()`) and, where the class persists, `Save()` round-trip and `ToBsonDocument()`.
- Follow project conventions: `[TestInitialize]` / `[TestCleanup]` state restoration, `Assert.Inconclusive` for missing seeded data, and `Assert.IsNotNull( x, "Precondition: ..." )`.

issues.title: Update a customer Employee with provided Employee ID values
issues.description:
Erin Burdette of a customer emailed the ORBIT team with CSV files containing the Employee ID for their employee. The overall task is to take these CSV files and update the Employee with their Employee ID.

Technically, these CSV files must be used to query the ORBIT PROD database for a Employee's PersonaId by their Enterprise Email. The result of this should be a new CSV file containing just the PersonaId and Employee ID. Finally, this new CSV file can be used in the new Employee ID Upload feature in the ORBIT Web UI Settings area.

issues.title: Fix Notification SMS and Mobile Check-In Verification
issues.description: As of now the verification boxes allow you to just enter anything to verify your number, these should require the actual code sent to the device. The resend verification code button and verification success message send via sms to the Mobile Check-In number instead of the correct Notification SMS number.
